title: Vivaldi: birdsong between the refrains
work: The Four Seasons · Spring, RV 269 — I. Allegro
question: How do the violin’s birdsong and the returning orchestral refrain change between these two performances?
intro: Vivaldi’s Spring starts with strings greeting the season in E major. Bird calls interrupt them, a storm sweeps through, and the same refrain keeps returning. John Harrison recorded it live with the Wichita State University Chamber Players in 2000; the second performance comes from Musopen.

recordings.label: John Harrison · Wichita State University Chamber Players · Robert Turizziani
recordings.note: Harrison’s live, unedited performance at Wiedemann Recital Hall, Wichita State University, on 6 February 2000.

recordings.label: Modena Chamber Orchestra
recordings.note: A solo violin and chamber orchestra, issued by Musopen as part of The Four Seasons.

passages.label: The opening refrain
passages.note: The strings announce spring with short, repeated phrases in E major.

passages.label: Birds answering birds
passages.note: The violins trade trills and short rising and falling calls, with space between one bird and the next.

passages.label: Half the refrain returns
passages.note: Only the refrain’s second phrase returns, gathering the scattered violin calls back into the orchestra.

passages.label: The storm breaks
passages.note: Rapid violin figures break into the refrain; the storm drives the music through B major towards C♯ minor.

passages.label: Back towards E major
passages.note: The refrain starts in C♯ minor and works back to E major; the strings recover the opening’s familiar tune.

passages.label: The final refrain
passages.note: The orchestra brings back the refrain in E major, rounding off the solo violin’s last flights.
